title: From equitable to promissory estoppel
summary: Equitable estoppel can prevent a person from asserting a position inconsistent with an earlier representation or conduct on which another person reasonably relied to their detriment.
notes:
The casebook uses this background to explain the development of promissory estoppel. Traditional equitable estoppel often concerns a representation about an existing fact; promissory estoppel concerns a commitment about future conduct. Ricketts uses the older terminology while enforcing a future promise after the granddaughter changed her position. Distinguish the historical language used by the court from the later doctrinal label.

Ricketts is part of the transition: a gift promise induced departure from employment, and the court prevented reliance on lack of consideration. The notes trace historical categories in which courts protected reliance, including family land improvements, gratuitous bailments, and charity. The modern section 90 formulation makes the forward-looking promise explicit; the historical labels alone do not settle its elements.
